scenario.summary: ARTEX is a Go-based autonomous AI penetration testing framework used by threat actors like Storm-0940 and Salt Typhoon to automate reconnaissance, web exploitation, and lateral movement. The framework coordinates multiple LLM agents to execute off-the-shelf tools at machine speed, progressing from initial access to cloud privilege escalation and mass data exfiltration in minutes.

meta.rationale: Focus on servers running web applications and Linux-based developer workstations where ARTEX-compatible tools and interpreters (Node, Python) are expected but high-frequency use is rare.
meta.hypothesis: An automated agent is performing high-frequency tool execution to conduct reconnaissance and dump credentials from sensitive files like .env or /etc/shadow at machine speeds.

hunt.name: Machine-Speed Agent Tooling and Credential Harvesting
hunt.description: This hunt targets the endpoint activity of the ARTEX agentic AI framework. ARTEX uses a Go-based backend to orchestrate multiple LLM agents that execute offensive tools (like nc, sqlmap, and hydra) in rapid succession. This hunt identifies the 'machine-speed' execution pattern by baselining interpreter frequency within one-hour windows and corroborating that activity with access to sensitive credential stores like environment files and OS-level shadow files, alongside DNS signals to known exfiltration sites. An agent then evaluates the combined telemetry to distinguish between legitimate automation and an autonomous penetration testing framework.

config.beyond_detection: A standard detection rule might trigger on 'sqlmap.exe', but ARTEX's durability comes from rotating tools and techniques at speed. This hunt pivots between tool discovery, a baseline for execution frequency (the 'machine-speed' signature in 1-hour windows), sensitive file access, and DNS exfiltration signals, providing the context an analyst needs to identify autonomous automation rather than a single tool hit.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{artex_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(replace(process_name, '/', '\'), '\', ',')) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify any execution of the specific offensive binaries and networking tools mentioned in the report, handling full paths.
config.expected_signal: Rows indicating that penetration testing tools like sqlmap or hydra are running. The query treats every directory and filename in the path as a potential match against the tool list.

primitive_config.label: Search for ARTEX-associated offensive tools
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{artex_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(replace(process_name, '/', '\'), '\', ',')) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Rows indicating that penetration testing tools like sqlmap or hydra are running. The query treats every directory and filename in the path as a potential match against the tool list.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H', time) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS launch_count, COUNT(DISTINCT process_name) AS unique_tools, MIN(time) AS first_launch, MAX(time) AS last_launch FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{interpreters}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(replace(process_name, '/', '\'), '\', ',')) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name, hour_bucket HAVING launch_count > 20 ORDER BY launch_count DESC
config.description: Identify hosts running a burst of commands through common interpreters within a 1-hour window, suggesting AI-driven automation.
config.expected_signal: A stack-count of hosts showing dozens of interpreter launches in a single hour. Legitimate CI/CD pipelines might appear here and must be filtered by user context.

primitive_config.label: Baseline for machine-speed interpreter use
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, user_name, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H', time) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS launch_count, COUNT(DISTINCT process_name) AS unique_tools, MIN(time) AS first_launch, MAX(time) AS last_launch FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{interpreters}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(replace(process_name, '/', '\'), '\', ',')) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, user_name, hour_bucket HAVING launch_count > 20 ORDER BY launch_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: A stack-count of hosts showing dozens of interpreter launches in a single hour. Legitimate CI/CD pipelines might appear here and must be filtered by user context.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, actor_user_name, file_path, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{harvest_targets}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(replace(file_path, '/', '\'), '\', ',')) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.env%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Check if processes are accessing files known to contain secrets, capturing the process name for correlation.
config.expected_signal: Processes reading sensitive files like /etc/shadow or .env. The query is path-aware and captures the acting process to facilitate correlation with the tool-lead step.
